title: Augmented free integer chains on ordered tuples
statement: For a set $Y$ and $m\geq0$, let $T_m(Y)=\mathbf Z[Y^m]$ be the free integer module [def-weil-pbc-free-module] on all ordered length-$m$ tuples, with repetitions allowed and the specified unit basis. Thus $T_0(Y)$ is canonically $\mathbf Z$ on the unique empty tuple; $T_{q+1}(Y)$ is the chain group in homological degree $q\geq-1$, with zero groups below degree $-1$. Define the additive deletion map $d_m:T_{m+1}(Y)\to T_m(Y)$ by $d_m[y_0,\ldots,y_m]=\sum_{i=0}^m(-1)^i[y_0,\ldots,\widehat{y_i},\ldots,y_m]$, in particular $d_0[y]=[\varnothing]$. For a map $f:Y\to Z$ define $T_m(f)$ by applying $f$ to every coordinate. For $b\in Y$ define $C_{b,m}:T_m(Y)\to T_{m+1}(Y)$ by prefixing $b$, including $C_{b,0}[\varnothing]=[b]$. For a group $Y$ define left translation $L_{g,m}=T_m(y\mapsto gy)$, trivial at length zero. All maps are extended additively from the specified bases; the boundary out of the empty degree and maps from the lower zero groups are zero.
